fact.title: Getting started with enrollment timing
fact.question: How does first Medicare enrollment timing work?
fact.text: For most people first becoming eligible at 65, the Initial Enrollment Period is a 7-month window: the 3 months before the birthday month, that month, and the 3 months after. The date coverage begins also depends on when enrollment happens and which enrollment period applies. Current health insurance matters: Medicare.gov checks the kind of insurance, whether job-based coverage comes from current employment, and employer size before giving timing guidance. Do not turn this general explanation into a personal start date, deadline, eligibility decision or permission to delay Part B. A first-of-month birthday has special start-date rules.
fact.summary: The sign-up window and coverage start are different; current insurance helps identify the relevant timing questions.
